sentence: твоя́ лову́шка для ра́ков гото́ва к вы́лову
translation: your crayfish trap is ready to fish

translation: it's time to collect the crayfish meat
explanation: пора́ = nominative. ра́ковые = acc. plural(not alive)

sentence: живо́тные с твое́й фе́рмы скуча́ют по тебе́
translation: the farm animals miss you
explanation: живо́тные = nom. plural. твое́й = gen. fem.

sentence: твоя́ ути́ная лову́шка гото́ва к вы́лову
translation: your duck trap is ready to fish
explanation: вы́лову = noun

translation: it's time to milk the cows
explanation: коро́в = either acc. or gen.

translation: mary the builder will leave soon
explanation: уе́дет = уе́хать

sentence: торопи́сь, е́сли всё ещё хо́чешь порабо́тать над диза́йном фе́рмы
translation: hurry up, if you still want to work on your farm's design
explanation: торопи́сь = торопи́ться. хо́чешь = хоте́ть. диза́йном = inst. sing.

translation: the event chicken valley has begun
explanation: начало́сь = past neuter. нача́ться

translation: everything's mature, it's time to collect the crops
don't forget to claim/get your daily gift
explanation: забу́дь = imperative perfective. забы́ть

translation: the candle maker recieved a mastery star
explanation: мастерства = gen.

translation: the pasta kitchen building is finished
we went to the cinema
explanation: пошли́ = perf. past. пойти´. кино́ = acc. sing.

translation: we sat in the last row
explanation: Мы (pronoun: we), сиде́ли (verb: past tense, to sit), на (preposition), после́днем (adjective: prepositional, last), ряду́ (noun: prepositional, row).

translation: it wasn't interesting for me to watch it
explanation: Мне (pronoun: dative), бы́ло (verb: past tense, to be), неинтере́сно (adverb: not interesting), смотре́ть (infinitive: to watch), его́ (pronoun: it).

translation: my friend fell asleep
explanation: : Моя́ (pronoun: possessive, my), подру́га (noun: nominative, friend), засну́ла (verb: past tense, to fall asleep).

translation: the movie lasted three hours
explanation: Фильм (noun: nominative, movie), шёл (verb: past tense, to go/last), 3 (numeral), часа́ (noun: genitive, hour).

translation: We went to the cinema
explanation: Мы (pronoun: we), пошли́ (verb: past tense, to go), в (preposition: to/into), кино́ (noun: accusative, movie/cinema).

translation: The movie started at seven in the evening
explanation: Фильм (noun: nominative, movie), нача́лся (verb: past tense, to start), в (preposition), 7 (numeral: seven), ве́чера (noun: genitive, evening).

translation: Finally, the movie ended
explanation: Наконе́ц-то (adverb: finally), фильм (noun: nominative), зако́нчился (verb: past tense, to end).

translation: It was ten in the evening
explanation: Бы́ло (verb: past tense, to be), 10 (numeral), ве́чера (noun: genitive, evening).

sentence: Мы с Мари́ей вы́шли из кинотеа́тра
translation: Maria and I left the cinema
explanation: Мы (pronoun: we), с (preposition: with), Мари́ей (noun: instrumental, Maria), вы́шли (verb: past tense, to exit), из (preposition: from), кинотеа́тра (noun: genitive, cinema).

translation: It was dark outside
explanation: На (preposition: on), у́лице (noun: prepositional, street), бы́ло (verb: past tense), темно́ (adverb: dark).

sentence: Мы вы́звали такси́ и пое́хали домо́й
translation: We called a taxi and went home
explanation: Мы (pronoun), вы́звали (verb: past tense, to call), такси́ (noun: accusative), и (conjunction: and), пое́хали (verb: past tense, to go by transport), домо́й (adverb: home).

sentence: За́втра мы опять пойдёт в кино́
translation: Tomorrow we will go to the cinema again
explanation: За́втра (adverb: tomorrow), мы (pronoun), опя́ть (adverb: again), пойдёт (verb: future, will go), в (preposition), кино́ (noun: accusative).

translation: We will watch another movie
explanation: Мы (pronoun), бу́дем (verb: future auxiliary, will), смотре́ть (infinitive: to watch), друго́й (adjective: accusative, another), фильм (noun: accusative).

translation: I arrived at the station
explanation: Uses the feminine past tense verb прие́хала (arrived by transport) and the noun вокза́л in the accusative case

translation: I have a ticket for the train
explanation: A common construction У меня́ (At me) is used to indicate possession, followed by the noun биле́т (ticket) and по́езд (train).

sentence: Я е́ду в го́сти к подру́ге в друго́й го́род
translation: I am going to visit my friend in another city
explanation: Е́ду denotes traveling by vehicle. The phrase в го́сти implies a social visit, requiring the dative case for the person (подру́ге).

translation: I looked at the board
explanation: Uses the verb посмотре́ла (looked) followed by the preposition на and the accusative case.

translation: My train has not arrived yet
explanation: Uses the negative particle ещё не (not yet) and the verb прибы́л (arrived).

sentence: Я села́ на скаме́йку и ста́ла ждать
translation: I sat on a bench and started to wait
explanation: Села́ (sat down) takes the accusative скаме́йку; ста́ла (became/started) pairs with the infinitive ждать (to wait).

translation: People were sitting nearby
explanation: Ря́дом is an adverb meaning nearby, while сиде́ли is the plural past tense of сиде́ть (to sit).

translation: They were also waiting for the train
explanation: Demonstrates the usage of то́же (also) and the verb жда́ли (imperfective past).

translation: They had big suitcases
explanation: Similar to У меня́, У них indicates possession; бы́ли is the plural past of to be.

translation: I heard an announcement
explanation: Услы́шала (heard) is a perfective verb followed by the object in the accusative case.

translation: My train has arrived
explanation: Confirms the arrival of the train using the past tense прибы́л

sentence: Я взяла́ рюкза́к и пошла́ на платфо́рму
translation: I took my backpack and went to the platform
explanation: Взяла́ (took) and пошла́ (went on foot) are both past tense verbs

translation: There were many people there
explanation: Uses the adverb мно́го (many/much), which requires the noun to be in the genitive case (люде́й).

sentence: Я зашла́ в свой ваго́н и села́ у окно́
translation: I entered my carriage and sat by the window
explanation: Зашла́ implies entering on foot; у окна́ indicates proximity.

translation: The train started moving
explanation: Пое́хал describes the commencement of travel

sentence: Я смотре́ла в окно́ и ду́мала о подру́ге
translation: I was looking out the window and thinking about my friend
explanation: Смотре́ла and ду́мала are imperfective past verbs, showing ongoing actions during the train ride.
